Subfactors, index and finite-depth classification

Smooth representations and compression onto the tracial tower

A representation can enlarge both algebras in a subfactor inclusion. A finite common basis still controls its basic construction, even when the larger algebras are neither finite nor factors. We construct that expected tower explicitly. We then show how the canonical tracial tower can produce a compatible hypertrace on a smooth representation. The latter argument has two precise hypotheses: an injective projection onto the tracial tower and its bicommutant identity. Generation supplies the first hypothesis; the second remains a separate mathematical condition. Every nonzero physical corner and positive real amplification also preserves the full all-smooth representation amenability condition. Explicit finite matrix induction and return maps retain all tower levels and allow singular compatible hypertraces. An explicit downward expected tunnel gives a compatible hypertrace directly from generation. Together with SA.7, this proves the full original strong-amenability/generating-tunnel equivalence for proper finite-index inclusions with separable predual. The full original global-finite-approximation/strong-amenability equivalence also holds without ambient separability. Exact finite-prefix matching and a separate factorial-core construction preserve its original finite-set scope.

The finite partial basis is Theorem 3.2, and the ordinary trace and cup identities are Theorems 4.1–4.2 and Proposition 4.3. The generating inclusion used below is Theorem 60.5. Normal tracial expectations, standard left/right commutation, matrix positivity and the bimodularity of a unital positive projection onto a C*-subalgebra are the operator-algebra prerequisites already used in lessons 3, 49 and 60. For normal state extension we use the exact existing-course Theorem 10.1 of The double commutant theorem: every positive normal functional on a concrete von Neumann algebra is a sum of square-summable vector functionals. Its complete proof applies to arbitrary Hilbert spaces.

The human source is Sorin Popa, Classification of amenable subfactors of type II, Sections 2.1–2.3 and 4.5, printed pp. 191–197 and 223–225. We give the finite matrix construction and keep the GNS compression explicit. The injective projection constructed from finite-dimensional generation below also preserves the right trace, which permits an exact corner normalization.

Theorem 61.16 — strong amenability and generating tunnels. For a proper finite-index inclusion of II₁ factors with separable predual, the following are equivalent:

  1. The inclusion is strongly amenable in the original representation sense of SA.1.
  2. Some ordinary tunnel is generating.
  3. Every prescribed finite ordinary tunnel prefix, with its actual cups, has a generating continuation.

No extremality or finite depth is assumed.

Proof. The full forward theorem SA.7 gives , and follows by choosing a prefix. For , Theorem 61.15 gives original all-smooth representation amenability. The larger actual core of the generating tunnel is , a factor, so the core is ergodic. These are exactly the two conditions of SA.1–SA.2.

Theorem 61.16 proves the strong-amenability/generating-tunnel equivalence in Popa's Theorem 4.1.2 and Theorem 5.1.1 at their stated separable scope. The separate physical bicommutant identity in the canonical upward tracial completion remains a distinct assertion. The proof here neither establishes that identity nor assumes it as a hypothesis of the generating-to-amenability direction.

All this remains inside the given original inclusion. The core has separable predual, but it need not equal the possibly nonseparable ambient factor.

The original global approximation and strong-amenability equivalence

Theorem 61.20. For a proper finite-index inclusion of II₁ factors, with no separability assumption, the following are equivalent:

  1. Original all-smooth representation amenability and ergodic actual core.
  2. Amenability relative to one actual ordinary core, together with ergodicity of that core.
  3. Condition (G).
  4. Condition (G) after every prescribed finite ordinary prefix.

These are the full first three clauses of Popa's Theorem 4.1.2, with the stronger exact-prefix formulation included.

Proof. The full core-square admission SA.3–SA.5 gives . For , the exact relative hypertrace/Følner criterion 49.2 and the finite approximation theorem 60.4 apply to that actual factorial larger core. Those proofs impose no ambient separability. Theorem 61.18 gives , and is immediate.

Suppose now (G). Choose an arbitrary smooth normal faithful nondegenerate representation . For each finite and , select the finite tunnel from (G). The finite downward construction of Corollary 61.14 and Theorem 61.15 gives a normal state on this same , restricting to , satisfying , and central over its actual terminal . Its finite version of (61.55) gives

Direct the pairs by inclusion of and decreasing . A cofinal weak-* cluster in is an -central, -invariant state with the original trace marginal. It need not be normal. For every fixed , the net eventually includes and its bound tends to zero. This proves the full all-smooth amenability quantifier over the original, possibly nonseparable . No countable replacement of its finite test sets has been made.

Independently, Theorem 61.19 constructs an actual ergodic core. These are exactly the two conditions in item 1. Thus , completing the equivalence.

At separable predual, Theorem 61.16 also identifies these conditions with an actual generating ordinary tunnel and the original standard-part realization. The argument above supplies the full finite-set equivalence without that extra assumption. The general nonextremal physical bicommutant in the canonical upward tracial completion remains a separate unproved assertion here.

Exercise 61.15 — two different limiting arguments at nonseparable predual

Why does Theorem 61.19 use a countable diagonal while the final state argument in Theorem 61.20 uses a directed net? Explain exactly what each limit proves.

Solution. Every actual ordinary core is generated by countably many finite-dimensional relative commutants. Its chosen matrix-unit bases form a countable dense set. Repeated finite unitary averages of those bases force the center expectation of that particular core to be scalar, proving ergodicity. This does not approximate every element of a nonseparable along one sequence.

For the original amenability quantifier, (61.64) is imposed on every finite subset of the whole . The net is indexed by all such subsets and all positive tolerances. Each fixed eventually appears, so every cofinal state cluster centralizes it and preserves the original expectation and trace marginal. The cluster may be singular. Thus one limit constructs a separable actual factorial core; the other proves the full all-smooth state condition on the original ambient factor. Neither is an infinite reflected trace comparison or a proof of the physical bicommutant identity.
